programme.sub-title: Into The Woods/Krumm Gets The Dreaded Nolox

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters

programme.sub-title: Mayberry U.F.O. / I Dream of Snorch with the Long Golden Hair

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: On a beautiful spring day, Ickis, Krumm and Oblina frolic in a fresh pile of garbage only to find that they have inadvertently boarded a garbage barge headed for the wide open seas.

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Oblina infiltrates the human race in a "human suit." When the suit malfunctions, and she thinks she's human, Ickis and Krumm have to rescue her. While above the ground, a puppy saves Ickis from being run over.
programme.sub-title: Monster Who Came in from the Cold / Puppy Ciao

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Oblina, long used to being the star pupil, finds herself challenged to the limit by a gifted transfer student from another dump. Ickis steals a magicians hat, assuming that its powers will make him the most popular monster at the academy.

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: When a human designer realeases a new fragrance, the monsters discover it works as a toxic gas against them. Oblina's not superstitious, but when she steps on a slug her luck changes.

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: When the viewfinder stops working, Ickism Oblina and Krumm tell very different versions of the same scare. Ickis eats a seed that grew on a tree, and soon finds he's turning into a tree himself.

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: The Gromble teaches students about their proud heritage. A famous artist creates a huge statue entitled "Fear," which is actually a clay sculpture of a looming Ickis.
programme.sub-title: History Of The Monster World, Part One / Fear Thy Name Is Ickis

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Ickis is chosen by mysterious forces as the monster who quests for the holy pail - the most sacred of monster objects. When the city mayor declares a "Dump the Dump" recycling effort, the lack of garbage causes a crisis at the Academy.
programme.sub-title: The Quest For the Holy Pail / Garbage In, Garbage Out

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Desperate to avoid being strapped to the viewfinder, Ickis attemps to dismantle it - and the viewfinder escapes. Ickis and Oblina find themselves monster-sitting a swollen, helium-voiced and cranky Krumm when he swallow a helium tank.
programme.sub-title: A Room With No Viewfinder / Krumm Rises To The Top

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: The Gromble insists that Ickis come up with five scares in one day. Ickis lets a huckster clone him five times so he can get the job done. Simon the Monster Hunter is hot on the trail of Bigfoot, who turns out to be one of the Gromble's ex-students.
programme.sub-title: The Five Faces of Ickis / Bigfoot, Don't Fail Me Now

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: The festival celebrates the shedding of skins that each monster must undergo as he or she moves from childhood to adolescence. Ickis, Krumm, and Oblina sneak into Simon's house to scare him.
programme.sub-title: Festival of the Festering Moon / Simon's Big Score

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Oblina, overstudying to the point of exhaustion for an upcoming exam, sneezes her brain out of her head. Ickis, Krumm, and Oblina go on a scare in an abandoned building. They spot four gargoyle heads sticking out of the wall.
programme.sub-title: Who'll Stop the Brain? / Cement Heads

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Ickis discovers a remote control helicopter in the dump and uses it to scare humans from long distance. When the Gromble dumps his obnoxious nephew on Ickis, Krumm, and Oblina, the only way they can find to keep him quiet is to tell him a story.
programme.sub-title: Ickis and The Red Zimbo / Oblina and the Three Humans

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Ickis, Krumm, and Oblina are saddled with babysitting the Gromble's infant nephew -- Bomble. A new carnival opens near town and The Gromble is insulted and outraged by one of its attractions -- the "Monsters Are Fun" ride.

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Ickis is in the middle of a botched scare on the viewfinder when The Gromble sees the dreaded "Jolly Rooter Sewer Service." Oblina is left in charge when the Gromble goes off to the Annual Academy Teachers Convention, and power goes to her head.
programme.sub-title: Out of the Past / Ship of Fools

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Ickis, Krumm and Oblina go for a romp in the sewer, tossing one of Krumm's eyes around in a game of catch. When Oblina is invited home for the weekend, Ickis and Krumm come along and discover that being rich is no walk in the dump.
programme.sub-title: Eye Full of Wander / Lifestyles of the Rich and Scary

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Krumm misplaces an eyeball for the seventh time in a week, and decides what he really needs is a head. Ickis' boasting gets the better of him after he sits through a cutesy movie, just to prove that he can.
programme.sub-title: Krumm Gets Ahead / It's Only A Movie

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Ickis, Krumm, and Oblina pick a mild-mannered Englishmen to scare, thinking it will be a piece of cake. A wacky radio DJ announces that $50,000 has been hidden in the dump. Soon humans are swarming there and the monsters can't get rid of them.
programme.sub-title: You Only Scare Twice/Less Talk, More Monsters

programme.title: Aaahh!!! Real Monsters
programme.desc: Ickis, Krumm, and Oblina discover an old sixteen milimeter "B" movie in the dump, which they watch constantly despite the Gromble's protests. Ickis falls head over heels in love when he spots the screeching hook-nosed Judy from a Punch and Judy show.
programme.sub-title: Fistful of Toenails / Blind Love, Monster Love

programme.title: What Would You Do?
programme.desc: Using hidden cameras, host John Quiñones observes and comments on how ordinary people behave when they are confronted with dilemmas that require them either to take action or to walk by and mind their own business. Various scenarios are created that force people to make split-second -- and often surprising -- decisions, and variations of the situation (such as changing the genders, races or clothing of the people involved) are often featured to see if different reactions are elicited. Examples of situations on the show include a waitress being harassed by her boss, and a drunken valet trying to park cars.
Two suitcases containing human remains are discovered along a Wisconsin highway, sending shockwaves through the community.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Today Dog and the family are back in Colorado and are about to make one of their most exciting captures ever. On his search he'll encounter a felon with history of violence and an alleged affection for sawed-off shotguns.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: There's no rest for the righteous and nobody knows this better then the Dog. He is committed to saving his new friend's bail bonding business, and now must race against time to bring a rogues gallery to justice.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog is in Denver helping Bobby Brown to track down a fugitive with a long rap sheet. But unfortunately they have no picture of the felon to work with, so the challenges are big on this one.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: When Leland learns that one of his clients with a reputation for stealing has lost her co-signer and could be ready to run, Dog and the crew hop a plane to the Big Island.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog's got a twofer on his hands, but the cases couldn't be more different. The first is a woman whose family wants her back in jail, the other is a former choirboy whose family ties are strong.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: This fugitive has a bad reputation and a knack for running from the law. The pursuit has Dog and team traveling through an urban dystopia of suspicion, false leads and mistrust.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: This fugitive is hard to pin down in Honolulu's downtown district--moving from hostel to hotel to apartment high-rise. But as the hunt evolves, Dog discovers that this alleged burglar isn't the only family member wanted by the law.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: No one becomes a bondsman overnight and even the members of Dog's team know there is always more to learn. So when Duane Lee cuts a felon a little too much slack about checking-in and then goes missing, Duane Lee knows he's gonna get schooled.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog and his team fight the war on ice - crystal methamphetamine - on many fronts. They appear on a special anti-drug float in a parade. Then they go after bail-jumping Pana, a convicted drug dealer.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: It's the day before Valentine's Day and love is in the air at Da Kine Bail Bonds--but not for Tapi who has failed to appear in court on theft charges. Dog's plan is to have Leland knock on Tapi's door with a Valentine's gift to draw her out.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog juggles his job and family responsibilities at the same time. He leads the search for Robert, a low-level drug dealer who makes money by selling hedge clippings as marijuana and broken Macadamia nuts as crack.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog and the team have girl trouble in this case. Krystal jumped bail and seems to have vanished into the high plains of Colorado. To make matters worse, she's running with her lover (and bond co-signer) Carrie.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Only in Dog's world would a bantam fighting cock, a pregnant daughter, and a jungle safe house go together. And don't forget the mopeds as well a group of hostile squatters on government land! They're all part of the hunt for an elusive criminal.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog knows that it is better to give than to receive, so when a fellow bondsman grieving for his recently departed spouse requests his help, he jumps into action. Studying the fugitive's file the team uncovers a surprising fact.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog has two fugitives to catch, and he gets help from the unlikeliest sources--the fugitives' mothers. First, Ginger's mother wants to revoke her daughter's bond because 18-year-old Ginger is selling drugs and running wild.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog and the team go after Kandice, AKA Candy, AKA Suga, a stripper who didn't make her court appearance. They convince one of her friends to lure her to a supermarket parking lot, where Dog has an easy time fetching the fetching young thing.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog always wants to share the wisdom he has collected on the streets with the fugitives he captures. But today he's going to do double duty! His son-in-law Travis (and trainee bondsman) is also in need of some knowledge.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog is going to be the keynote speaker at the annual Profession Bail Agents convention in Las Vegas, but before he leaves he's got to clear two cases from his docket--Heidi and Stephanie. Heidi is a check forger who's failed to make a court appearance.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog faces a tough personal and professional situation when he must hunt down his friend, Ili, who has helped him on many busts. But now Ili's on the other side of the law. She's didn't come to court to answer charges that

programme.desc: It hurts Dog to see people who after years of walking the straight and narrow, suddenly lose their way. But today's case is a member of the law enforcement community who has recently gone astray, and that truly troubles the Dog.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Plans by Barnaby to renew his wedding vows at the church of St Michael's in Badger's Drift, are quickly put on hold when the body of Richard Bayly, a local developer, is found decapitated in his own home. The detective is left mystified as to why anyone would kill a man who had only been given weeks to live, after being recently diagnosed with a brain tumour. As he and Troy attempt to find out, they soon encounter a hotbed of corruption and property feuding occurring within the village as the body count rises and the mystery deepens.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: When Carla Constanza - the face of Brazil's leading cigarette brand for Monarch Tobacco - is found strangled in the infamous Strangler's Wood, Barnaby and Troy not only find themselves investigating her murder, but three identical unsolved murders of innocent girls from eight years before.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Cully's latest boyfriend, Nico, decides to shadow Troy in preparation for a TV role he recently got, but gets more hands-on experience than he expected when investigations into a slashed painting at a museum in Aspern Tallow, a 17th century portrait of Royalist Jonathan Lowrie, are overshadowed by the murder of his descendant, Marcus Lowrie. It isn't long before Barnaby and Troy, with Nico's assistance, find themselves dealing with mysterious, ghostly events, escaped criminals, and a museum trustee who has more to them than meets the eye.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Hector Bridges, a local magistrate, is infuriated when one of his geese is stolen, just as two bands of travellers arrive in Martyr Warren. Although Barnaby and Troy are called in to deal with the theft and later dissuade him from forcefully evicting the travellers from the village, they soon have a murder on their hands, when a short while later Bridges is killed with his own shotgun. It quickly transpires that many in the village had hated the magistrate, who lied, bullied, and committed many an injustice, leaving the detectives determined to find who among them had pulled the trigger after Bridges pushed them past their breaking point.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: The demise of the Shirewell patriarch sparks a vicious inheritance dispute when eldest son Lucian announces plans to break up an estate that's been in his family for centuries.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: When the author of a book that sparked a nationwide treasure hunt is found dead, Barnaby and Winter must unravel the cryptic clues to find the killer among a group of dedicated seekers.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: After a pet detective turns up dead inside the kennel of a dog he was searching for, Barnaby and Winter are drawn into the world of dognapping, cat seduction, and animal investigation.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Sleepy Goodman's Land is known as the Greenest Village in Midsomer. But when the entire village is bought by a Texas oilman, a string of grisly murders ensues.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: A series of murders in Midsomer St Claire seem to be inspired by macabre images on a medieval fresco recently discovered in the church crypt. programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: When wealthy farmer Martin Strickland is covered in truffle oil and mauled to death by a wild boar, the investigation leads to restaurant Wyvern House and its tyrannical celebrity chef Ruth Cameron. programme.title: Midsomer Murders

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, the crew heads to Colorado to field test Winchester’s new Supreme Long Range ammunition—engineered for hunters who demand precision at extended distances. Featuring the BC Max bullet, built with a high ballistic coefficient, heat-resistant tip, and match-grade components, this round is designed for flatter trajectories, reduced wind drift, and devastating terminal performance.After confirming zero and studying real-world drop and wind deflection at the range, the team heads into Colorado’s rugged backcountry in pursuit of mule deer and elk. With fresh snow, steep canyons, and long shooting lanes, the terrain offers the perfect proving ground to see how the new bullet performs under pressure. From close-range opportunities to challenging cross-canyon shots, this hunt puts the technology—and the hunters—to the test in one of the West’s toughest landscapes.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, Winchester athletes Kim Rhode and Desiree Edmonds share what it takes to compete at the highest level of clay target shooting. From the pressure of national competition to the routines that build confidence, they reveal how preparation, mental focus, and years of dedication lead to success. The transcript emphasizes that managing pressure is a learned skill, supported by consistent routines and trust in dependable equipment like Winchester AA shotshells. As the two champions train, mentor the next generation, and reflect on the journeys that shaped their careers, the episode celebrates more than trophies. With Kim's Olympic legacy and Desi's Hall of Fame induction, the passion, perseverance, and commitment to excellence that continue to inspire shooters across the country.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, Winchester team members and employees meet up at the Keefer Brothers property in Missouri for a multi day deer camp. Along for the ride are outdoor editors Scott Ergas and Dave Hurteau. Chris and Casey are on the search for some large bucks, as well as showing the people at the camp a great time and what deer season is all about.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, the crew travels to Wyoming for a three-day waterfowl hunt with the Teton Mallard Company. Hunting everything from narrow creeks and sloughs to larger river channels, they adapt to changing weather, shifting winds, and unpredictable bird movement as they pursue ducks against the stunning backdrop of the Teton Range.Throughout the hunt, the team puts Winchester's Last Call Double Shot ammunition to the test, showcasing its stacked payload technology in real hunting conditions. As opportunities come and go, they break down how the combination of plated steel and tungsten delivers increased pellet counts, hard-hitting performance, and confidence on challenging shots.From slow mornings to exciting evening flights, every hunt brings new lessons, memorable retrieves, and the reward of time spent in the blind. Set in one of the West's most scenic waterfowl destinations, this episode highlights the preparation, adaptability, and precision it takes to make the most of every opportunity in the field.

In this premiere episode, Rush Maltz jumps aboard a skiff with local captain Jake Leon to explore the shallow, clear waters that make Key Largo one of the most iconic fisheries in the Florida Keys. From stealthy presentations to explosive eats, this is inshore fishing at its finest. With unmatched access to the Atlantic Ocean, Florida Bay, and Everglades National Park, Key Largo truly lives up to its reputation as the gateway to paradise. From snook and sea trout to elusive bonefish, this episode sets the tone for a season built around world-class fishing, local eats, and unforgettable destinations. Get ready for the first stop of your Florida Keys experience.

programme.title: Local Knowledge
programme.desc: The next stop on our Florida Keys adventure brings Rush Maltz to the legendary waters of Islamorada — a destination known for its laid-back island vibe, world-class fishing, fine dining, and easy access to the reef. Joining locals Jimmy Hendrix and Jordi Hortensi, the game plan is simple: check in by boat, chase fish, eat well, and go dive. From kite fishing the reef to fresh seafood and great company, this episode is all about experiencing the true rhythm of a Florida Keys vacation.

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: The positive impact made by the shooting sports and recreational shooting to people across our country can’t be measured in just one story, so we have three. In Florida, Olympian Dania Vizzi trains at her home shooting facility and talk about how she went from ballerina to one of the best shotgun shooters in the world. In Nebraska, firearms instructor Thea Van Syoc has used the disciplines of competitive pistol shooting and training to help shape her life. Finally we’ll take a look into the National African American Gun Association and learn how one day at the range for Phillip Smith created the fastest growing firearm organization in the United States.

programme.title: Stories of the Hidden Worlds
programme.desc: Dharavi is a locality in Mumbai, India, considered to be one of the world's largest slums. Dharavi has an area of just over 2.1 square kilometers and a population of about 700,000. Dharavi is one of the most densely populated areas in the world. The Dharavi slum was founded in 1884 during the British colonial era and grew in part because of an expulsion of factories and residents from the peninsular city center by the colonial government, and from the migration of poor rural Indians into urban Mumbai. For this reason, Dharavi is currently a highly multi-religious, multi-ethnic, and diverse settlement. Dharavi has an active informal economy in which numerous household enterprises employ many of the slum residents leather, textiles, and pottery products are among the goods made inside Dharavi.

programme.title: Deltas of the World
programme.sub-title: Irrawaddy Delta: The Magical World of Mangroves
programme.desc: The Irrawaddy Delta in southern Myanmar is home to the most diverse mangrove forests in the world. The forests serve as natural protection against cyclones that regularly strike the region. The Irrawaddy's widely branching tributaries not only provide schools of fish and rich nutrients, but also function as the most important transport route for the people living in the delta. The greengrocer couple U Tin Hlaing and Daw Khin Lay supply the villages downstream with their fresh produce. But they do not go any further than the Meinmahla Kyun Wildlife Sanctuary. From that point on, the river becomes increasingly turbulent, too dangerous for their small, flat boat. The sanctuary is home to a variety of animal species including the rare Irrawaddy dolphins, saltwater crocodiles, birds of prey such as black kites and brahminy kites, migratory birds such as spoon-billed sandpipers, woodcocks, great cormorants and various anatids. Ranger Lha Soe Win and his colleagues regularly patrol the nature reserve to monitor the animal population and make sure the mangroves are no longer illegally logged for firewood. Since the 1970s, the mangrove population has declined by more than 60 percent, with dramatic consequences for the inhabitants of the delta. Cyclone Nargis, the most devastating cyclone to date, claimed the lives of around 130,000 Burmese in 2008. Together with scientists from the conservation charity Flora and Fauna International, the rangers are working on reforesting the mangroves to restore their function as a natural barrier in the future.

programme.title: Deltas of the World
programme.desc: Hardly any other area is as unspoiled as the Yukon Delta in western Alaska. This fascinating network of swamps and river arms looks like a landscape at the beginning of mankind. Only 25,000 people live in this barren region, which is almost as big as Greece. Most of these inhabitants are indigenous and belong to the ethnic group of the Yupik. They make their living on the steep banks of the Yukon River. And in their villages, built on piles to protect them against flooding, you can see the effects of climate changes on nature - and on the community life of the indigenous population. On the trail of the national fish of Alaska, the salmon, the film follows the Yukon River and follows moose hunters, migratory birds and scientists who do research in the delta.

programme.title: Moody McCarthy
programme.desc: Moody was born “Matthew” in Syracuse, NY, into a rambunctious household with six siblings. (They're Irish...somebody had to get a nickname.) He began doing comedy in 1992 and was soon hired by Syracuse's top morning radio show to cover sports and write jokes, his first loves. After six years of working the road, Moody moved to New York City. This millennium has been good to Moody: he's also been featured on Last Comic Standing, Star Search (the 2003 reboot), and America's Got Talent. He's a regular at the best clubs in the land (including the world famous Comedy Cellar) and can be heard on SiriusXM. Moody's material is described as original but universal, and smart without being trite. Couple that with a disarming stage presence & in-the-moment chops, you'll see why he's earned the admiration of his peers for his ability to “go up cold” and turn any setting into a hot room. From corporate outings to pubs, this versatile performer will brighten any event.

Soon, a royal decree is issued for the Bunwon to produce pottery for the common people, and Gwanghae sets out to find Jeongi.

He promises Jeongi that if she succeeds, he will elevate her to the rank of master potter.

Gwanghae petitions the king to lift the Chief Scholar's exile, but Seonjo misinterprets the request as a threat to royal authority. Seizing the moment, Inbin plots to frame Gwanghae for treason by forging his letter. As Jeongi departs on Gangcheon's errand to mine white clay, Gwanghae mounts his horse and races after her.

programme.title: Goddess of Fire Ep.23

programme.title: Back To School
programme.desc: When the NEXO-Knights are sloppy in a fight with Jestro, Merlok 2.0 sends them back to the Knights' Academy. Not only for a brush-up but to find out what Jestro is after in its hallowed halls. As they Knights battle Jestro – in a somewhat haphazard and lazy way – they discuss the fact that Jestro never wins and that they're always getting over on him. Despite defeating the jerky Jester and his evil Book, Merlok 2.0 discovers that something about the attack on the village is tied to the Knights' Academy. It looks like that's where they'll strike next. It wouldn't hurt for the Knights to go “back to school” to watch for Jestro and for some refresher training. Merlok is sure Jestro wants something at the Academy, but he doesn't know what it is. The Knights are very much “fish out of water” at the academy, even with the “cool kids” – Robin and Ava – showing them around. The next generation of Knights is being taught to integrate the NEXO-Magic of Merlok into their fighting techniques and these kids are good (so good, they initially kick the lazy, know-it-all Knight's butts!) Their old principal, the ever-ornery Headmaster Brickland, sets them straight: they're all still slackers, and they better get their acts together (especially Lance!) The Knights take shifts as “library helpers” much to the delight of the old squirebot librarian, MARGE. They're convinced Jestro is after a book…isn't he always after a book? When Jestro attacks, the Knights help organize the students and there's a big fight in the Academy Library versus Jestro and his Monsters. They drive Jestro off without letting him steal any books! Victory! But as Jestro leaves, we see him holding what the Book of Monsters really wanted: a snow globe with a castle in it that was sitting on the librarian's desk. In the Lava Lands, Jestro throws the snow globe into a volcano and it frees the massive Castle of Monstrux from its snowy magic prison

programme.title: Con el Odio en la Piel
programme.desc: Un sheriff y sus malévolos secuaces humillan y asesinan a los mexicanos que viven en un pueblo fronterizo de Texas.

programme.title: La Lucha con la Pantera
programme.desc: Tres muchachas confundidas con el sexo y el amor cometen errores llevados por el deseo carnal.

programme.title: Operativo de alto riesgo
programme.desc: Una médica forense descubre quienes son sus verdaderos amigos, durante la investigación de un caso de alto riesgo.

programme.title: Lo Negro del Negro
programme.desc: Un hombre empleado del gobierno aprovecha su posición para su beneficio apoderándose de una inmensa fortuna.

programme.title: Vámonos para la feria
programme.desc: Un hombre decide que es hora de que sus dos hijos se casen. Para eso, acude a su compadre, que tiene dos bellas hijas.

programme.title: Romance en Puerto Rico
programme.desc: Una joven escapa como polizón en un barco que viaja a Puerto Rico para no casarse con un millonario.

programme.title: Dos valientes
programme.desc: Martín, un pistolero, es asesinado, pero antes de morir pide que le oculten su identidad a su hijo. Este corre peligro cuando asiste a su funeral.

programme.title: Hoy He Soñado con Dios
programme.desc: Una mujer tiene tres hijos muy diferentes: una hija fracasada, el otro un boxeador furtivo y su hijo el sacerdote.

programme.title: El corrido de María Pistolas
programme.desc: Un hombre finge estar del lado de los ricos para enterarse de sus planes, y así los revolucionarios venzan en un ataque.

programme.title: Reencuentros
programme.desc: Al morir su hermano de leucemia, un niño pobre toma su bicicleta y emprende un viaje a la ciudad en busca de su padre.

programme.title: Cuna de valientes
programme.desc: En colegio militar, cuatro jóvenes se hacen amigos y juntos comparten mucho, pero solamente dos de ellos se gradúan.

programme.title: Las Pobres Ilegales
programme.desc: Una joven huye de su casa por su padrastro y se va a los EE.UU., donde descubre el abuso a los indocumentados.

programme.title: Milagro en el Barrio
programme.desc: Un niño ciego y el hijo de una rica familia se hacen amigos aún en contra de la voluntad de la madre del último.

programme.title: El Llanto de los Pobres
programme.desc: Un joven ilegal es acusado por un robo que no cometió, purga una condena en la cárcel donde sueña con volver a su país.

programme.title: Desvestidas y alborotadas
programme.desc: Una bella mujer es abandonada por su marido en su luna de miel, y los hombres en el hotel andan detrás de ella.

programme.title: Entre Cornudos te Veas
programme.desc: Una mujer va de vacaciones y es asediada por un deportista mientas su esposo coquetea con las clientas de su negocio.

programme.title: La Lucha con la Pantera
programme.desc: Tres muchachas confundidas con el sexo y el amor cometen errores llevados por el deseo carnal.

programme.title: El fin de un imperio
programme.desc: El teniente del batallón de Rurales, José Antonio Navarrete, es considerado héroe y enemigo de los imperialistas, quienes raptan a su gran amor para atraerlo e imponerle sus condiciones políticas.

programme.title: Me llaman violencia
programme.desc: Una mujer logra escapar de los asesinos de su padre, mientras huye conoce a un hombre que le ofrece protección.

programme.title: Bello amanecer
programme.desc: La espectacular belleza de una isleña que despierta entre los pescadores las más ardientes y locas pasiones.

programme.title: Mi nombre es Gatillo
programme.desc: Un hombre llamado el "Gatillo" solo tiene violencia en su sangre y su vida está controlada por las armas.

programme.title: Impaciencia del corazón
programme.desc: Un capitán herido es llevado a un pequeño pueblo y una joven lo cuida. Al final dos mujeres se enamoran de él.

programme.title: Muertes anunciadas
programme.desc: Un niño busca venganza por la muerte brutal de toda su familia, a manos de una banda de asesinos.

programme.title: La Dinastía de Drácula
programme.desc: Drácula despierta de su tumba después de dormir por tres siglos y reclama más víctimas para su reino.

programme.title: Los dos hermanos
programme.desc: Un hombre rico y poderoso está casado con una mujer mucho más joven, la cual tiene un amante.

programme.title: El Deseo
programme.desc: Dos hermanas están enamoradas del mismo hombre, pero una de ella sufre una enfermedad incurable.

programme.title: Limosneros con garrote
programme.desc: Dos músicos y comediantes quedan en la bancarrota, encuentran una bebé en una canasta y deben trabajar para poder conservar a la niña.

programme.title: Mi Borinquen querida
programme.desc: Tras un accidente, una joven hereda una gran fortuna, por lo que un hombre se aprovecha del amor que despertó en ella.

programme.title: Tú y la mentira
programme.desc: La esposa de un cantante se vuelve vedette e intenta engañarlo con un cantante venezolano, que resulta ser su amigo.

programme.title: Juan Charrasqueado
programme.desc: Un ranchero regresa a su pueblo, les gana en un juego de cartas a unos jugadores profesionales y escapa con su novia.

programme.title: De Tal Palo Tal Astilla
programme.desc: Dos recién nacidos son confundidos al nacer y los padres se sienten mutuamente traicionados hasta que todo se aclara.

programme.title: La Bruja
programme.desc: Una mujer fea toma un brebaje que la vuelve hermosa temporalmente, pero todo el que la vea en estado de fealdad, morirá.

programme.title: El casto Susano
programme.desc: Un hombre puritano viaja a la capital para visitar clubes nocturnos y se presenta como soltero, pero, para su sorpresa, se encuentra allí con su esposa.

programme.title: En la hacienda de la flor
programme.desc: Un joven quiere ir a una hacienda y su madre le advierte que desde que mataron a su padre esta ha quedado maldita.

programme.title: Yo fui novio de Rosita Alvírez
programme.desc: Un charro se emborracha y llora al recordar a su novia, una coqueta mujer que terminó muerta en manos de uno de sus pretendientes.

programme.title: Arsenio Lupin
programme.desc: Un millonario contrata a Sherlock Holmes para que atrape a Arsenio Lupin, un ladrón elegante que roba a los ricos para repartir los botines que consigue entre los pobres.

programme.title: El que con niños se acuesta
programme.desc: Un mensajero de telégrafos es rechazado por los padres de su novia y ambos deciden escapar juntos a la capital.

programme.title: El hombre sin rostro

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty sows rocket, harvests chillies and tomatoes, and demonstrates how to take semi-ripe cuttings. Frances Tophill meets a head gardener in south London who's started gardening sustainably.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty Don has advice on how to successfully store an apple crop so it will last through winter and explains why he thinks it high time wall flowers came back into fashion. With tomatoes now over, Monty clears his greenhouse.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty revels in the roses in his garden, harvests honey and gives advice on the maintenance of geraniums as well as planting others for summer ground cover. Rachel de Thame shows how spaces can be transformed by adding seasonal containers.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With Halloween approaching, Monty takes stock of his pumpkins and squashes, plants up alpines and shows how to divide a large fern to create new plants. Meanwhile, Adam Frost and Advolly Richmond visit Hever Castle in Kent.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty Don tackles the perennial problem of what to grow in the shade beneath a tree, Carol Klein has a look at the crocosmia, and we meet a gardener in Derbyshire who has spent a lifetime growing and showing gladioli.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty Don prepares the flowering borders for winter and makes a bonfire, Carol celebrates our berry-laden hedgerows, and Rachel visits Julian Clary in his garden.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A celebration of people who are growing their own, from vegetables to flowers, across the UK. At Longmeadow, Monty shares tips and advice on how to get the most out of bargain plants. Meanwhile, Joe visits an extraordinary food project in Bristol.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty's in the jewel garden showing which plants need protection from the elements now and which ones can be left until after the first frosts. He also plants out berried shrubs to help feed wildlife in the winter, and harvests pumpkins.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: In the cottage garden, Monty is moving a rose which has outgrown its space and in the vegetable garden he gives advice on what to plant now for spring. He also finds out more about the mysterious world of earthworms.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty catches up with summer maintenance in his wildlife garden and recommends plants for deep, dry shade under trees, as well as giving advice on what to plant now for late summer harvests.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty Don tackles autumn lawn maintenance tasks, Carol Klein is looking at burnets, and we meet a man who's dedicated himself to a North American prairie favourite, the echinacea.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty Don gets going with some autumn garden maintenance whilst looking back over the year and reviewing his borders, checking which plants have done well and which haven't. Carol Klein is at Glebe Cottage continuing work on her new raised beds.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty Don harvests apples, pears and quince and plants indoor bulbs, we meet a Northern Irish daffodil breeder, and Carol Klein travels to Wales to explore the Eupatorium with a passionate gardener who has a rare and spectacular collection.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty's thoughts turn to spring when he gives recommendations for bulbs to plant that will thrive in pots. He also shows how to prune summer fruiting raspberries. In Norfolk, Frances Tophill visits a gardener who at 97 still gardens every day.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty is preparing for spring colour as well as harvesting pumpkins and squashes. Carol Klein visits comedian Joe Lycett at home, and together, they plant up a container packed with layers of colourful bulbs.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With autumn on the horizon, the seasonal planting of bulbs for spring-flowering begins at Longmeadow. Frances Tophill meets a gardener whose allotment is filled with traditional and exotic vegetables and Toby Buckland visits The Newt in Somerset.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With autumn fast approaching, Monty is preparing the borders for the change of seasons and looking ahead to spring. Adam Frost and Advolly Richmond visit a glorious historic garden in North Yorkshire - Scampston Hall.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: There's plenty to do to prepare for the season to come, and Monty Don is clearing out spent crops and mulching his asparagus. Joe Swift's been to visit Wayne and Geraldine Hemingway, to see how they combine sustainability with their designer-style.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty harvests his spuds and sows seeds for autumn veg. He also shows how to get plants for free by taking cuttings.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty plans for next spring when he plants some early-flowering wildflowers and gives his recipes for the compost mixes he uses to take successful cuttings. Nick Bailey continues his quest for the South African origins of some summer bulbs.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty propagates succulent plants, revisits his container vegetable garden, and gives advice on how to get a good crop of pumpkins. Adam looks a new garden at RHS Hyde Hall in Essex, and Rachel visits a garden of vibrant colours in Wiltshire.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty gets going in his vegetable garden sowing seeds for a bountiful summer and growing some more unusual vegetables as well as recommending varieties of summer bulbs to plant in spring. Plus, Mark Lane creates a floral celebration in a container.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Despite the slow awakening of the garden, there are still plenty of jobs to be getting on with. Monty begins to divide ornamental grasses, gives advice on what to do with containers which are past their best, and plants up a colourful alpine trough.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Celebrate the best of spring gardening with Monty at Longmeadow, and visit the RHS Malvern Spring Festival to see 2018's hottest garden designs and the season's must-have plants. At Longmeadow, Monty plants herbaceous perennials for summer colour.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty elevates his cottage garden borders by adding plants to give height and drama, and rejuvenates the design of the grass borders by adding evergreen plants grown from cuttings. Carol Klein's plant of the season is the delicate dog's tooth violet.

programme.title: Monty Don's Spanish Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across Central Spain. He begins at the vast, imposing palace and garden of the Escorial before heading for Madrid, Toledo, other parts of Castile and finally Valencia.

programme.title: Monty Don's Spanish Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don is in the south of Spain, visiting gardens that show how this part of the country has evolved thanks to influences from visitors and settlers from ancient to modern times.

programme.title: Monty Don's Spanish Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don travels across northern Spain, visiting gardens across this vast and diverse landscape that changes from an Atlantic to a Mediterranean climate as he journeys from Galicia to Catalonia.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don travels from the north-west coast of Scotland to the north-east coast of England, from historic reconstructions to modern re-inventions. He visits some of the most inhospitable places in the country and finds gardens that are flourishing.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across some of the country's landscapes, heading across the north of England to Northern Ireland. Here, Monty sees the ingenuity, passion and determination of British people to garden and create gardens, no matter what the canvas.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across the middle of the country, from Wales to Norfolk. He comes across gardens for gnomes, much-loved, well-tended allotments and extravagant gardens that bankrupted their owners.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don explores the most densely populated part of the country, London and the home counties. He visits some of London's gardens, including a special one on a barge, as well as a beautifully restored garden close to where he grew up in Hampshire.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across the south-west of the country to visit some of Britain's most exotic gardens. On this journey, Monty also goes to some of the country's most historic gardens, as well as some challenging contemporary ones.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty sows rocket, harvests chillies and tomatoes, and demonstrates how to take semi-ripe cuttings. Frances Tophill meets a head gardener in south London who's started gardening sustainably.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: At Longmeadow Monty is planting bulbs in pots and around the garden for an explosion of spring colour. Carol Klein travels to Yorkshire where she has a close look at the enormous colour range and form of a late season perennial, the salvia.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty cuts back and divides spring flowering plants, and gives advice on the pruning, dead-heading and staking of roses. Joe Swift and Adam Frost help a couple of gardeners turn a neglected area of their garden into a useable space.

programme.title: Monty Don's Japanese Gardens
programme.desc: Monty continues his travels to learn about the art of Japanese stonemasonry and the famous tea ceremonies and their accompanying gardens, before finally taking a lesson in the delicate art of traditional flower arranging.

programme.title: Monty Don's Japanese Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don returns to Japan during the fiery blaze of autumn. He visits the three great gardens of Japan to learn how they protect the garden from the coming winter and learns how the Japanese are weaving nature into their concrete urban jungle.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don is in and around Rome, a power base of emperors and popes, to explore gardens that are among some of the most extravagant and flamboyant ever created in history.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don visits gardens in Florence and the Tuscan countryside, discovering that renaissance gardens were created as works of art.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don is in Naples visiting some of the most sublime, romantic retreats in southern Italy. After the formality of the green gardens around Rome and Florence, Monty seeks out idyllic horticultural gems set against the scenery of the Amalfi Coast.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.sub-title: The Veneto, Lucca and The Lakes
programme.desc: Monty Don concludes his garden tour of Italy in the wealthy north where, in the Veneto and Lucca, extravagant pleasure gardens were created for flirtation and fun.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Cosmology takes the entire universe as its subject, not just its form, structure and contents, but also the manner of its birth and evolution; looking at the origin of cosmology in creation stories and its relation to the journey ahead.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Introducing the hierarchy of structures in the universe; from planets to stars, galaxies, galaxy clusters and larger groupings of galaxies called the cosmic web; light travels at a finite speed, looking far away also means looking far back in time.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Discussing cosmic properties; the universe is lumpy at the scale of galaxies and galaxy clusters; at larger scales, it is smooth and similar in all directions; this property of homogeneity and isotropy is called the cosmological principle.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: The most familiar constituents of the universe are atomic matter and light; neutrinos make up another component; 96 percent of the universe is dark energy and dark matter; the relative amounts of these constituents changes as the universe expands.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Taking a trip through the universal timeline from the big bang to a future of ever-accelerating expansion; the eight key stages between them include the condensation of atoms, the birth of the first stars and the formation of galaxies.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Astronomers overlap techniques of "distance ladder" to determine distances in the universe; triangulation works for nearby stars; observers use pulsating stars for farther objects, the rotation of galaxies and a class of supernova explosions.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Measuring the Doppler shift of galaxies in the early 20th century; observations reveal that they all were moving away from Earth; the more distant ones move faster, proportional to distance; this is the Hubble Law, implying the initial "big bang."

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Professor Whittle defines distances in cosmology; the three important distances to consider is the emission distance when the light is set out; the current distance, when the light arrives; the distance the light travels.

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.desc: Illustrating scientific debates over the rise of humans; the ancestry casts Ramapithecus out; witnessing fossil evidence and molecular evidence, working both together and independently; explaining some of anthropology's most complex issues.

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.desc: Discovering and debating over fossil remains of a possible Homo ancestor, Australopithecus afarensis, in 1970; following the story from the perspective of the key personalities involved, scientists Don Johanson and Richard Leakey.

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.desc: Discovering the 4.4-million-year-old remains of Ardipithecus ramidus; debating whether it is a true hominin or not; suggesting a mix between an effective climber and walking bipedally; examining the fossil and genetic evidence of this "ground ape."

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.desc: A human's brain separates them more from apes than any other anatomical feature; investigating the gradual increase in hominid brain size; fossil skulls revealing facts about blood circulation; shedding light on brain size and skull structure.

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.desc: Exploring the link between diet and morphology in Australopithecus robustus and Africanus; the teeth and jaws of these two species offer fierce debates about dietary hypotheses; adaptive differences between robust and gracile hominids.

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.desc: Wondering whether Africa or Asia is closer to human origins; drawing on the ideas and theories of prominent scientists like Charles Darwin, Ernst Haeckel and Louis Leakey; learning how scientists trace the origin and evolution of the genus Homo.

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.sub-title: An Ape's View of the Oldowan
programme.desc: Tools mark a major step in evolution, but even chimpanzees can make and use tools; Professor Martin offers a detailed picture of early stone toolmakers, illustrating some of the primitive tools found in parts of Africa.

programme.title: The Rise of Humans: Great Scientific Debates
programme.desc: Fossil records reveal that Homo habilis serves as a transitional marker between Australopithecines and the rest of the genus Homo; Homo habilis has the anatomy to be ancestors of the genus Homo yet not exist at the right time in evolutionary history.

programme.title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
programme.desc: The horrors of Nazi Germany are one hallmark of World War II; pondering how ordinary German citizens find themselves participating in such heinous events; going inside the propaganda machine of Hitler's Germany; seeing how it targets the youth.

programme.title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
programme.desc: The origins of World War II lie in Asia in 1931; tracing the invasion of 1937 and the Rape of Nanjing; witnessing the events through the eyes of a Chinese soldier and a Japanese journalist, young men who bear witness to the flesh and blood of battle.

programme.title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
programme.desc: In addition to the story of people, World War II is the story of technology; perhaps nowhere is this more apparent than the tanks Germany uses to barrel across Poland and France in "lightning warfare"; how new technology defeats the old ways of war.

programme.title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
programme.desc: Wartime Warsaw offers a gateway to the darkest events of the war; bearing witness as the city's Jews are rounded up and put in the ghetto, where the specter of disease and starvation always looms; stories from several of the ghetto's inhabitants.

programme.title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
programme.desc: If war is a gamble, then a strategy is key to success; a survey of why strategy is important; looking at World War II's "Operation Torch" as a case study for how the military should be used as an instrument of policy.

programme.title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
programme.desc: A systematic look at what makes Thucydides perhaps history's first great strategist; his analysis of the Peloponnesian War; the political origins of the war; the Spartan and Athenian leadership; the social and moral implications of war.

programme.title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
programme.sub-title: Thucydides as a Possession for All Time
programme.desc: Joining a debate over the efficacy of the Sicilian Expedition; turning to the Melian Dialogue; the debate between realists and neoconservatives over the conduct of war; considering how this debate still plays out in contemporary America.

programme.title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
programme.sub-title: Sun Tzu's the Art of War
programme.desc: Sun Tzu's writing is popular in the modern world; the historical context for "Master Sun's Military Methods"; an overview of Sun Tzu's strategy for war, which is to be efficient, avoid protracted wars and value the commander's intellect and skill.
